Folks — I pulled the export and attached the CSV (usage-export-2027-07-24_2027-07-30.csv). Quick summary of what I see:

- There are ~37.9M tokens attributed to org_id: archscope-prod during 2027-07-26 02:00:00 -> 2027-07-26 06:15:00 UTC.
- The majority (~75%) of those requests are tagged with route: /v1/embeddings and show a client_user_agent header that matches a one-off ingestion job we commonly see when customers run large re-index jobs.
- However, ~12% of the rows have api_key: sk-live-arch-zz-xyz which appears to be a production key; the remaining 13% have api_key: sk-stage-arch-qa.

Preliminary hypothesis: a scheduled ingest job in ArchScope's staging namespace used a production key for a short window (likely a leaked credential or a rotated key not propagated). That would explain the backdated production attribution.

VAT implications: because the org is EU-registered and the billing entity is Redwood US LLC, we currently treat the usage as B2B reverse-charge when the customer supplies a valid VAT id. The current invoice included VAT because the billing contact did not (yet) provide the VAT registration number at invoicing time. If we apply a retroactive reclassification (credit the backdated overage and reissue the invoice) we will remove the VAT portion for those lines — final amount and VAT adjustment will be provided after reconciling exact token counts per api_key.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Provisional credit: offer a provisional credit equal to the disputed overage (estimate €18k) to stop collection while we reconcile.
2) Full reconciliation: finalize token attribution per api_key and produce an adjusted invoice with VAT corrected.
3) Security follow-up: Rafael to confirm whether ArchScope rotated keys on 2027-07-26 and whether they issued any automated replays.

I attached the raw CSV and a short pivot sheet in the Drive link. If we confirm staging used a prod key, I recommend full credit for the disputed window and a procedural note for the customer about key separation.
